name: らーめん 鴨to葱 渋谷宮益坂店 (Ramen Kamo to Negi Shibuya Miyamasuzaka)

claims.text: The ramen's finishing tare is soy-based; sources describing the shop as a "duck broth soy sauce ramen" specialist imply standard (wheat-containing) shoyu rather than a wheat-free tamari.

name: ラーメンまこと屋 渋谷センター街本店 (Ramen Makotoya Shibuya Center-gai Honten)

claims.text: The menu displays a QR code linking to a full allergen chart covering the eight major mandatory allergens (egg, dairy, wheat, buckwheat, peanut, shrimp, crab, walnut) plus soy, beef, chicken and pork, though a blogger who visited with an egg/dairy-allergic child still recommended confirming specifics with staff in person before ordering.
Provides an in-store QR-code allergen chart at the table/register covering major allergens rather than leaving customers to guess ingredients.

name: ラーメン龍の家 新宿小滝橋通り店 (Ramen Tatsunoya Shinjuku Otakibashi-dori)

claims.text: The shop's tare/seasoning is shoyu (soy-sauce) based tonkotsu, which in standard Japanese ramen preparation contains wheat; no wheat-free tare or noodle alternative is documented for this shop.

Menu listings show a coarsely-milled nihachi (二八) soba — a wheat/buckwheat blend, not 100%-buckwheat — plus a shrimp tempura rice bowl with a wheat-flour batter, indicating standard shared-kitchen preparation rather than gluten-free handling.
The menu includes vegetable-forward dishes such as stir-fried mixed vegetables and morning glory (kang kong / water spinach) alongside the standard Thai and Vietnamese offerings.
Traditional fugu preparations (ponzu-dipped tessa/sashimi, techiri hot pot dipping sauce) rely on standard soy-based sauces that typically contain wheat; no wheat-free soy sauce option is documented.

name: 背脂ラーメン チャッチャ亭 (Seabura Ramen Chaccha-tei)

claims.text: The broth is a pork-bone shoyu (soy sauce) base, and soy sauce in Japanese ramen shops is standardly wheat-based unless stated otherwise; no gluten-free or wheat-free tare was mentioned in any source.

name: Sensing Touch of Earth（センシング・タッチ・オブ・アース） (Sensing Touch of Earth)

claims.text: Plain hand-whisked organic matcha and French-press specialty coffee are simple, wheat-free beverages with no obvious hidden gluten source.
